slides.title: The math module
slides.main: Combinatorics from discrete math in one call: comb and perm.

body.text:
import math

print(math.sqrt(16), math.floor(2.7), math.ceil(2.1), math.trunc(-2.7))
print(round(math.pi, 4), round(math.e, 4), math.hypot(3, 4))
print(math.gcd(12, 18), math.lcm(4, 6), math.factorial(5))
print(math.comb(5, 2), math.perm(5, 2))
print(math.isinf(math.inf), math.isnan(math.nan))

slides.title: float error
slides.main: Never compare floats for exact equality: ask whether they are close enough.

body.text:
import math

print(0.1 + 0.2)
print(0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3)
print(math.isclose(0.1 + 0.2, 0.3))
print(2 ** 100, 2 ** 100 + 1)
Python ints are exact and of unlimited length.

slides.title: Rounding
slides.main: round goes to the nearest even; for output use :.2f, the number stays the same.

slides.title: Decimal
slides.main: Create from a string, not a float, or the error is already inside.

body.text:
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP

print(Decimal("0.1") + Decimal("0.2"))
price = Decimal("19.99") * 3
print(price)
print(Decimal("2.675").quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
print(Decimal(0.1))

slides.title: Fraction
slides.main: Fractions reduce themselves; limit_denominator finds the nearest simple fraction.

body.text:
from fractions import Fraction

a = Fraction(1, 3) + Fraction(1, 6)
print(a, a == Fraction(1, 2))
print(Fraction("3/4") * 2)
print(Fraction(0.75), Fraction(3.14159).limit_denominator(100))

slides.title: random
slides.main: The same seed gives the same “random” sequence: handy for tests.

body.text:
import random

random.seed(1)
a = [random.randint(1, 6) for _ in range(5)]
random.seed(1)
b = [random.randint(1, 6) for _ in range(5)]
print(a == b)
print(1 <= random.randint(1, 6) <= 6, random.choice("abcd") in "abcd")
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
random.shuffle(nums)
print(sorted(nums))
print(len(random.sample(range(10), 3)), 0 <= random.random() < 1)

slides.title: Simulations
slides.sub: Dice and the Monte Carlo method
slides.main: The more trials, the closer the result to the theory.

body.text:
import random
from collections import Counter

random.seed(7)
rolls = Counter(random.randint(1, 6) + random.randint(1, 6) for _ in range(6000))
print(rolls.most_common(1)[0][0])
inside = 0
n = 100000
for _ in range(n):
    x, y = random.random(), random.random()
    if x * x + y * y <= 1:
        inside += 1
print(round(4 * inside / n, 1))
The share of random points inside the quarter circle estimates pi.

slides.title: statistics
slides.main: A mean alone is not enough: the median resists outliers, and the spread shows variety.

body.text:
import statistics as st

data = [2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9]
print(st.mean(data), st.median(data), st.mode(data))
print(st.pstdev(data), round(st.stdev(data), 3))
print(st.median([1, 2, 3, 100]), st.mean([1, 2, 3, 100]))

slides.title: secrets and hashes
slides.main: Games and tests: random; passwords, tokens, access: secrets; the database stores a hash, not a password.

body.text:
import secrets
import hashlib
import string

token = secrets.token_hex(8)
print(len(token), all(c in "0123456789abcdef" for c in token))
alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
password = "".join(secrets.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(12))
print(len(password))
print(hashlib.sha256("password".encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16])

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.sub: round, Decimal from float, empty mean
slides.main: Money: Decimal from strings; passwords: secrets; comparing floats: isclose.

body.text:
from decimal import Decimal
import statistics

print(round(2.675, 2))
print(Decimal(2.675) == Decimal("2.675"))
print(int(-2.7), -7 // 2, 7 % -3)
try:
    statistics.mean([])
except statistics.StatisticsError as e:
    print("empty:", e)

2.67
False
-2 -4 -2
empty: mean requires at least one data point
